## 2. Hierarchy body — every syllabus sub-point
### Ecological pyramids and energy flow

Fill order per concept: definition → structure → process → significance (§3.2). Step-by-step numbered points, Pioneer style.

An **ecological pyramid** graphs a trophic property — number, biomass or energy — level by level, with producers at the base. The **10% law** (Lindeman): only about a tenth of the energy at one trophic level reaches the next; the rest is lost to respiration, waste and uneaten parts. Energy pyramids are always upright; the other two can sometimes invert.

**Concept flow — from trophic levels to the 10% law (study in this order)**

| Step | Concept | Key point |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Trophic levels | T1 producers → T2 herbivores → T3 carnivores → T4 top carnivores |
| 2 | Energy transfer | Only ~10% passes up; 90% lost to respiration, heat, waste |
| 3 | Pyramid of energy | ALWAYS upright — energy must shrink upward (2nd law of thermodynamics) |
| 4 | Pyramid of biomass | Usually upright; inverted in the open ocean (phytoplankton stand small but turn over fast) |
| 5 | Pyramid of numbers | Usually upright; inverted for one tree → many insects → parasites |
| 6 | Implication | Top predators need vast territories — the reason they are rare and vulnerable |

**The three pyramids — which can invert and why**

| Pyramid | Units | Can it invert? | Classic inversion example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Energy | kJ/m²/time | NEVER — always upright | — (energy is lost at every transfer) |
| Biomass | g/m² (dry weight) | Sometimes | Ocean: few phytoplankton grams support more zooplankton — fast turnover |
| Numbers | count of individuals | Often | One large tree feeds thousands of insects, which feed thousands of parasites |

## 6. Key terms and statements
Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).

**Worked example.** Producers fix 100,000 kJ/m²/yr. By the 10% law: herbivores get 10,000, first carnivores 1,000, top carnivores 100. To support one 200-kg tiger, the ecosystem must fix energy for tonnes of deer and hectares of grass. **Why it matters:** this arithmetic is why top predators need huge home ranges, why food chains rarely exceed 4–5 levels, and why eating lower on the chain (plants) feeds more people per hectare.

## 8. Summary and self-check
5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.

**Summary.** Energy shrinks ~10× at every step; the energy pyramid is always upright, biomass and number pyramids sometimes are not. The consequence: few top predators, short chains, and plants as the energy base of everything. **Self-check:** starting from 200,000 kJ at T1, can you compute T2, T3 and T4?

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Three pyramid types — number, biomass, energy; energy pyramid is ALWAYS upright (Lindeman 10% law); biomass inverted in the ocean (phytoplankton < fish standing crop at a moment); number inverted for a single tree's insects.
Trick 2: 10% law numerical: 10,000 J producers → 1,000 J herbivore → 100 J carnivore → 10 J top — one chain calculation earns the numerical mark.
Trick 3: Trophic level rule: an organism can occupy more than one level (human: primary + secondary consumer); only ~4–5 levels possible because energy dies out.
Trick 4: Standing crop = biomass at a given time; pyramids of biomass use standing crop — the definition line.
